title: What The Sitar Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 102bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal Indian philosophy absurdist
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The sitar starts before the light arrives
Five in the morning and already something comes alive
Seven strings in sympathy, the drone beneath the air
The sitar knows the distance between silence and a prayer

[Pre-Chorus]
I tried it once in a music shop in Perth
The man said "this takes twenty years" — for what it's worth

[Chorus]
What does the sitar know that I don't know?
The answer's in the raga and the way the feelings go
What does the sitar know at five AM?
It knows the space between the notes is where you find your zen
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The raga has a grammar that predates the written word
A map of human feeling that the fingers have transferred
There's a morning raga, evening raga, monsoon raga too
The sitar's been scheduling emotion longer than I knew

[Bridge]
Every bend of string is a philosophy
From Delhi to Mumbai to the sitar's memory
I sat with one for fifteen minutes, still no wiser
But the sitar probably expected that

[Outro]
Sitar knows… I do not know… the sitar knows
That's my boy
